decisions.decision: Forecast weekly demand per store and product
decisions.context: The system must produce retailer demand forecasts, and the brief specifies the forecast grain and cadence.

alternatives.label: Weekly forecasts per store and product
Weekly forecasts per product across all stores

chosen.label: Weekly forecasts per store and product

decisions.rationale: This directly matches the required forecast unit and cadence.
consequences: Outputs need store and product identifiers.

decisions.decision: Make past-week forecasts reproducible from versioned inputs and code
decisions.context: The brief requires forecasts to be reproducible for any past week, which requires retaining enough information to reconstruct a run.

alternatives.label: Version inputs, code, and run configuration

chosen.label: Version inputs, code, and run configuration

decisions.rationale: A saved output alone cannot reproduce a forecast; versioned run dependencies give the team a basis for replay.
consequences: Historical data and code references must remain available.
Retention duration and storage mechanism need definition.

decisions.decision: Validate candidate models before production promotion
decisions.context: The team wants to move new model ideas to production quickly without breaking the weekly run, so experimentation needs a controlled path to production.

alternatives.label: Validate candidates in an isolated promotion path

chosen.label: Validate candidates in an isolated promotion path

decisions.rationale: A separate candidate validation and promotion path balances iteration speed with protection of the scheduled run.
consequences: The promotion gate and rollback procedure need definition.
Candidate evaluation adds work to the pipeline.

decisions.decision: Have the three-person data science team own the pipeline end to end
decisions.context: The brief explicitly assigns end-to-end pipeline ownership to a team of three data scientists.

alternatives.label: Data science team owns the pipeline end to end

chosen.label: Data science team owns the pipeline end to end

decisions.rationale: This follows the stated ownership model; automation and simple operations are important given the team size.
consequences: Operational procedures should suit a small team.
Support and on-call expectations remain to be decided.

uncovered: Source systems, input schemas, and data quality rules
Forecast horizon and whether forecasts are updated within the week
Model family, feature design, and retraining schedule
Evaluation metrics and candidate promotion thresholds
Weekly run schedule, orchestration platform, and failure recovery
Production runtime, forecast consumers, and output interface
Artifact storage, versioning mechanism, and retention period
Monitoring, alerting, access controls, and privacy requirements
